changes: original_meaning 按古英语 rīsan 的 gloss 收为「起身，起床」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 按 Etymonline 编年（约 1200 年泛化、天体升起；约 1300 年水位上涨）说明泛化过程，替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "Old English risan \"to rise from sleep, get out of bed; stand up, rise to one's feet; get up from table\"... It is attested from c. 1200 in the senses of \"move from a lower to a higher position, move upward; increase in number or amount; rise in fortune, prosper; become prominent;\" also, of heavenly bodies, \"appear above the horizon.\" Of seas, rivers, etc., \"increase in height,\" c. 1300."
rise.mechanism_sentence: rise 在古英语里是「从床上、从座位上起来」：约 1200 年起，这个「起来」从人身上扩给了万物——太阳升、水位涨、数目增，全是往上。

semantic_path.how: 从『人由卧、坐而起』扩到一切『由低向高』：约 1200 年 rise 泛指上移、数量增长、地位上升，日月星辰『升过地平线』也归它；约 1300 年江河海水涨高同样用 rise（Etymonline 编年）——词库今义『上升；升起；增加』即此。

changes: original_meaning 前溯到日耳曼语源头 *raubō 的 gloss「战利品（尤指抢来的衣物）」：现行路径以古法语的复合 gloss 起步，埋没了与 rob 同源的关键一环（牛津明言 from the Germanic base of rob）。
semantic_path 重建三站，『战利品中的衣物』一桥按 Etymonline 的推测语气（Presumably the notion is）表述，不写成定论。
evidence: Etymonline: "robe (n.) \"long, loose outer garment...\" late 13c., from Old French robe \"long, loose outer garment\" (12c.), from a Germanic source (compare Old High German rouba \"vestments\"), from West Germanic *raubo \"booty\"... which also yielded rob (v.). Presumably the notion is of fine garments taken from an enemy as spoil, and the Old French word had a secondary sense of \"plunder, booty,\" while Germanic cognates had both senses; as in Old English reaf \"plunder, booty, spoil; garment, armor, vestment.\""
Etymonline: "From c. 1300 in reference to official vestments... The meaning \"dressing gown\" is from 1854"
Oxford: "from the Germanic base (in the sense 'booty') of rob (because clothing was an important component of booty)."
robe.mechanism_sentence: robe 与 rob（抢）同源，老底是日耳曼语的「战利品」：抢来的东西里衣裳最显眼，「抢来的衣裳」慢慢只剩「衣裳」——法语 robe 成了长袍，英语里又分去管礼袍和浴袍。
robe.original_meaning: 战利品（尤指抢来的衣物）

semantic_path.meaning: 战利品（尤指抢来的衣物）

semantic_path.how: 想来桥在这里（Etymonline 以推测语气提出）：战利品的重要组成是衣物（牛津同说），『抢来的衣服』褪去『抢』、只剩『衣服』——古法语 robe 12 世纪已指宽松的长款外衣，13 世纪末入英语。
长袍又分尊卑两路：约 1300 年起指法官、教士、行会成员的身份礼袍（1640 年代 the Robe 喻指法律界）；1854 年添家居的晨衣、浴袍义——从战场抢来的衣服，最后穿回了卧室。

changes: original_meaning 按古英语 rūh 的 gloss 收为「粗糙的；毛蓬蓬的」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 按 Etymonline 编年梳理扩展面（14 世纪中天气/海浪/言语、约 1600 年粗略义），替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "Old English ruh, rug- \"not smooth to the touch, coarse (of cloth); hairy, shaggy;\" of hides, \"undressed, untrimmed;\" of ground, \"uncultivated.\""

Etymonline: "Of stormy weather from mid-14c.; by late 14c. of turbulent seas, rude language, discordant sounds... The sense of \"approximate\" is recorded from c. 1600. Rough draft (or draught) is from 1690s."
rough.mechanism_sentence: rough 在古英语里是手上的感觉——「糙、毛蓬蓬」：14 世纪起，它管到天气、海浪、言语的不平顺，再到日子艰难、估算粗略——一个「糙」字，从指尖扩到了生活。

semantic_path.how: 触感蔓延到一切『不平顺』（比喻扩展）：14 世纪中 rough 形容狂暴天气、汹涌海面、刺耳言语，约 1600 年添『粗略、大概』义（rough draft『草稿』1690 年代）——手摸着不顺、日子过得坎坷、账算得不细，都是同一个『糙』；词库『艰难的』在这一支。

changes: original_meaning 按拉丁语 rudis 的 gloss 收为「粗糙的，未加工的；未开化的」（rudis 的更深词源来源作未定论，disputes 已登记，不写入路径）。
semantic_path 第二站 how 按 Etymonline 编年（14 世纪中指人粗野、14 世纪末至 16 世纪无礼义定型）说明由物及人的比喻，替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "rude (adj.) late 13c., \"coarse, rough, without finish\" (of surfaces), from Old French ruide (13c.) and directly from Latin rudis \"rough, crude, unlearned,\" a word of uncertain etymology, related to rudus \"rubble.\""

Etymonline: "The senses of \"ill-mannered, uncultured, boorish; uneducated, ignorant\" are from mid-14c.... The meaning \"marked by incivility, contrary to the requirements of courtesy\" is perhaps late 14c., certainly by 16c."
Oxford: "from Latin rudis 'unwrought' (referring to handicraft), figuratively 'uncultivated'; related to rudus 'broken stone'."
rude.mechanism_sentence: rude 是拉丁语 rudis——「没加工的粗坯、没开垦的荒地」：先说物粗糙，14 世纪起说人，没被文明打磨过，就是粗鲁无礼。
rude.original_meaning: 粗糙的，未加工的；未开化的

semantic_path.meaning: 粗糙的，未加工的；未开化的

semantic_path.how: 物的『没打磨』转到人的『没教养』（比喻）：14 世纪中 rude 形容人粗野无文、不懂规矩，14 世纪末至 16 世纪『违背礼貌、无礼』义定型——词库今义『粗鲁的』即此。
